content.text: {"verdict":"ready-with-fixes","claimsChecked":2,"findings":[{"severity":"major","target":"selection","problem":"Item 1 targets a single order ('LKTS(57) or LKTS(87)'). The cited excerpt calls these the smallest REMAINING cases, so other admissible orders are also open. Unless the 2009 book poses exactly these orders, constructing one of them is partial progress on the book's existence problem. That is the substituted-subproblem pattern the user ruled out, and the 'or' makes it a choice of one case.","evidence":"Selection item 1: 'LKTS(57) or LKTS(87)' and 'smallest remaining cases as of July 2026' (arXiv:2607.21521 Sec. 4, as read by parent). The bundle contains no book wording for item 1.","suggestedFix":"Quote the book's problem verbatim. If it asks for existence of LKTS(v) for all admissible v (or for a list of orders), make that the target and list every order still open per the 2026 source. Label any single-order construction as 'new case, not a solution of the book problem'. Recheck status for Jul-Oct 2026."},{"severity":"major","target":"selection","problem":"The evidence for open status and provenance is uneven and cannot support 'five still-unsolved problems from the 2009 book'. Item 1 has a dated excerpt (Jul 2026) for the specific orders. Item 2 has only an abstract-level 2025 statement about a broad version, and its main linear 0/1 case is settled per Schulz 2009 as read. Items 3-5 have no dated literature-status evidence: 'unresolved in our work' (3) and 'not yet certified / not pinned' (4, 5) are not evidence of openness. No item's book statement is quoted, so neither provenance nor absence of substitution can be checked.","evidence":"Item 3: 'remains unresolved in our work'. Item 4: 'open status of each is not yet certified'. Item 5: 'current status not yet independently pinned'. Item 2: only a chapter abstract.","suggestedFix":"For each item record three things: (a) the verbatim book statement; (b) the latest dated source asserting that exactly that statement is open, or else a dated search log labeled 'no resolution found; not proof of openness'; (c) the formal statement being attacked. Present unpinned items as 'status uncertified' or replace them. Do not call the set 'still unsolved' until (a) and (b) exist for all five."},{"severity":"major","target":"selection","problem":"Item 2's surviving question depends on formulation choices the bundle does not fix. Schulz's equivalence covers binary X, arbitrary c, a given feasible x0, and l1/linf. Beyond that, the remaining question depends on: how f(c,x) is given (explicit poly-time formula vs oracle); the parameter domain (bounds, integrality, sign); the distance (weighted l1/linf, l2/lp, Hamming, bottleneck Hamming); non-binary X; and whether x0 is supplied. In a model the agent chooses, a positive 'NP-hard forward / P inverse' example can be engineered or excluded by definition, so neither outcome answers the book's question. An abstract calling the 'broad' problem open does not identify a formal open statement. The bundle also does not show whether Schulz's equivalence covers distances beyond l1/linf, and I do not reliably recall.","evidence":"Item 2: 'separating the surviving nonlinear/parameter-domain formulation from the prior solved linear case and degenerate feasibility-only examples'. The only status source is an abstract.","suggestedFix":"Quote the book and Heuberger's original question. Write the surviving question with every modeling parameter fixed. Fix non-degeneracy criteria in advance, e.g. forward hardness must persist when a feasible solution is supplied, f must be poly-time evaluable, and 'natural' if the book requires it. Treat any result outside that fixed model as a side result."},{"severity":"major","target":"selection","problem":"Item 3's target conjecture is named but never stated, so the scoping of claim A and of the triangular counterexample cannot be checked against it. Missing pieces: (1) the implication, e.g. 'original weakly consistent => pooled weakly consistent'?; (2) quantifiers over rho and the error law, such as identifiability via E rho(eps - t) uniquely minimized at 0 and any moment or density conditions; (3) whose minimizer must be unique (original, pooled, or population); (4) whether p is fixed. Nothing shows the repeated-row pooled model is the book's formulation rather than a reformulation. 'Fresh i.i.d. errors' leaves the joint law across n unspecified.","evidence":"Item 3: 'Weak consistency conjecture for p>=2 and unique minimizers remains unresolved in our work'. No statement or book quote is given.","suggestedFix":"State the conjecture as one fully quantified sentence next to the book quote. Note that weak consistency depends only on the per-n law, so it is coupling-free, while any strong-consistency statement requires a specified coupling across n."},{"severity":"major","target":"selection","problem":"Item 4 is not well posed until the monomial order and the alphabets are fixed. A GSB always exists for any presentation and order: the full relation set is closed under compositions, and the reduced GSB is unique per order. So the real content is an explicit (finite or recursively described) reduced GSB for a specified order on a specified alphabet. Outside type A, the Artin-Garside alphabet (standard generators with Delta^(+-1)) has an evident analogue in every finite type, and BKL plausibly generalizes via the dual Garside structure. The type-A Artin-Burau alphabet, however, appears tied to the Burau/Markov presentation and the pure-braid combing structure. Whether a canonical analogue exists for every finite type is not established in the bundle (my recollection, uncertain: not for all types). I also recall (uncertain) that convergent simple-element presentations of finite-type Artin monoids are published, e.g. Gaussent-Guiraud-Malbos 2015, so that variant must not count. If the book asks for all finite types, a result for one type is a subproblem.","evidence":"Item 4: 'on the exact generator alphabets requested in the book' and 'simple-element Garside rewriting on an expanded alphabet (possibly already known)'. No order is given, and no alphabet definitions are given for non-A types.","suggestedFix":"Quote the book's alphabets, the types in scope, and the order. Define each alphabet for each type, or record that it is undefined there. Certify status per (type, alphabet, order) triple. Label single-type results as partial unless the book's question is per type."},{"severity":"major","target":"selection","problem":"Item 5's target statement is not fixed. 'Weakly E-unitary' and the Pastijn/semidirect product are undefined in the bundle. The glosses for 'locally r-orthodox' and 'seminormal band = every eBe regular' are paraphrases that have not been checked against Szendrei (2002) or the book. Status after 2002 is unknown.","evidence":"Item 5: 'Exact product definition/current status not yet independently pinned'. The bundle gives no definition of weakly E-unitary.","suggestedFix":"Copy the exact definitions (weakly E-unitary, the product, seminormal band, locally r-orthodox) and the embedding question from the book and from Szendrei 2002. Then run a dated status search that includes works citing Szendrei 2002."},{"severity":"minor","target":"claim-A","problem":"The proof is correct, but two caveats are mis-scoped. (i) 'Pooled = average of two strongly consistent estimators' holds for least squares with identical design copies (any p), not for general convex rho. For p=1, strong consistency of the fixed-stream pooled estimator still follows by a sandwich argument: a minimizer of a sum of two scalar convex functions lies between their unique minimizers. For p>=2 it is not automatic. (ii) 'Fresh i.i.d. errors' admits a third coupling: an independent error vector at every n. Under it even the ORIGINAL estimator in this example fails strong consistency, since P(A=1)=2^-j for each n, each block has 3*4^j independent n, and the second Borel-Cantelli lemma applies. So 'strong consistency' means something only after a coupling is fixed. Trivial point: uniqueness and the closed forms need n>=4 (j>=1).","evidence":"Claim A caveat: 'for TWO FIXED independent nested error streams, the pooled estimator is average of two strongly consistent estimators and is strongly consistent'.","suggestedFix":"Restrict the fixed-stream positive remark to least squares, or to p=1 via the sandwich argument. List all three couplings. State that claim A is a strong-consistency failure under the sliding single-stream coupling and has no bearing on weak consistency for nested or repeated designs. Add 'n>=4'."},{"severity":"minor","target":"claim-B","problem":"The argument is correct but is likely a rederivation. It proves that an STS(v) with an involution fixing exactly one point requires C((v-1)/2,2) to be even, i.e. v = 1 or 3 (mod 8). From memory (uncertain, verify before citing), this is the classical necessary condition for reverse Steiner triple systems (Doyen; Rosa; existence completed by Teirlinck, early 1970s): reverse STS(v) exist iff v = 1, 3, 9, 19 (mod 24). Since 87 = 15 (mod 24), it is excluded. Presenting this as a new obstruction would over-claim.","evidence":"Claim B uses only three things: the forced blocks through the fixed point, orbit triangles with 0 or 2 XOR-1 edges, and C(43,2)=903 being odd. It never uses resolvability or Z_85.","suggestedFix":"Check and cite the reverse-STS literature. State the result as 'no STS(87) admits an involution with exactly one fixed point', and derive the cyclic-model exclusion as a corollary."},{"severity":"minor","target":"claim-B","problem":"The stated scope is narrower than what is proved, and one step is implicit. (a) 'Block-pairs' requires g(B) != B for blocks avoiding the fixed point. This holds because an involution cannot leave invariant a 3-set containing no fixed point (odd size); the proof should say so and say 'g-image' instead of 'complement'. (b) The exclusion covers every one-fixed-point involution of the base STS. In the cyclic-transversal model it also covers any x -> c - x with u<->w that merely maps the base B to a translate B+t, because tau_(-t) composed with g is then an involutory automorphism of B with one fixed point. Add the elementary fact that the fixed points of an STS automorphism form a subsystem of order 1 or of order 1 or 3 mod 6. Then the other order-2 multipliers of Z_85, namely 16 and 69, combined with u<->w are also impossible, since they give 5 and 17 fixed points. These arguments do NOT exclude the variants that fix u and w: x -> -x (fixed set {0,u,w}, which must be a block), x -> 16x (7 fixed points), and x -> 69x (19 fixed points). (c) There is no such parity obstruction for 57: it has 28 pairs, C(28,2)=378 is even, and 57 = 9 (mod 24).","evidence":"Claim B: 'This only excludes that symmetry'. The proof uses only the STS axioms and the involution's fixed-point count.","suggestedFix":"State the exclusion at its proved strength and list the involutive affine ansatzes that remain. That way no search effort goes into excluded classes, and nothing beyond 'these symmetry classes are empty' is inferred, in particular not nonexistence of LKTS(87)."}],"difficultyAssessment":"Nothing in the bundle supports calling any of the five 'not too hard'. What can honestly be said: (1) Per a July-2026 excerpt, LKTS(57) and LKTS(87) are the smallest orders the known constructions have not reached. They are concrete, and a certificate found by search would be machine-checkable, but there is no evidence that a prescribed-automorphism exact-cover/SAT search will finish. For 87, claim B plus the fixed-subsystem condition shows that every order-2 affine symmetry swapping u,w is empty. 57 lacks that parity obstruction, which is not evidence that 57 is easier. Even success would settle one order, presumably not the book problem. (2) Item 2's main linear 0/1 case is already settled (Schulz 2009 as read). What remains depends on formulation, and a quick answer would most likely be a modeling artifact. (3) Item 3 has only side results: a strong-consistency failure under one coupling, and an unaudited broader-design example. The nested-design weak question for p>=2 is untouched, and its difficulty is unknown. (4)-(5) Exact statements and status are uncertified. These may already be solved, may be hard, or may be ill-posed for the requested alphabets and definitions. Honest description: 'five candidate problems from the 2009 book; open status documented for item 1 (as of 2026-07) and, at abstract level, for a broad version of item 2; difficulty unknown for all five.' No success prediction is warranted.","summary":"Both audited claims are mathematically correct as stated. Claim A: the following steps are all valid and together give limsup 1/2 and liminf -1/2 a.s.: the closed forms, Var=1/(2j), the j(j-1) intersection-degree bound, the Caro-Wei independent set of size >= 3*4^j/(j(j-1)+1), mutual independence from disjoint supports T_n, the exp(-3*2^j/(j(j-1)+1)) tail, the first Borel-Cantelli lemma across blocks, and A_j -> 0 a.s. with |B_n|<=1. The claim is correctly scoped as a strong-consistency failure under the sliding coupling, not a counterexample to nested weak consistency. Fixes: restrict the fixed-stream positive remark to least squares (or p=1), name the coupling, and note n>=4. Claim B: the forced-fixed-point lemma and the orbit-triangle parity count are correct (903 is odd), so no STS(87) admits an involution with exactly one fixed point. I believe, but have not verified, that this is the classical reverse-STS condition, so it should be cited. It excludes more symmetry classes than stated but says nothing about LKTS(87) itself or about 57. The main problems are in the selection. Item 1 targets one order of a presumably general existence problem. Open status is documented only for item 1, and at abstract level for a broad version of item 2. Items 2-5 need verbatim book statements and fixed formalizations before any 'full solution' could be recognized: the distance and model for 2, the conjecture statement and coupling for 3, the order and alphabets for 4, and the definitions for 5. The triangular-design weak counterexample was not embedded and is unaudited. This review does not establish that any of the five remains open."}
